title: PSI 内存压力：some/full、avg10/60/300 与 thrashing 判断
key_conclusions: PSI measures memory stall time, so it proves whether reclaim, compaction, or swap pressure is user-visible only when aligned with workload timelines.
some and full describe different impact scopes: some means at least one task is stalled, full means all non-idle tasks are stalled.
avg10, avg60, and avg300 separate interaction spikes, sustained scene pressure, and chronic background pressure.
Thrashing should be diagnosed with PSI plus refault, swap-in, vmstat, and Perfetto evidence, not PSI alone.
shallow_points: The article does not include real PSI samples from Android devices under controlled workloads.
It does not define numeric alert thresholds for different RAM classes or product latency targets.
It does not validate PSI availability and formatting across all Android versions and vendor kernels.
It does not include a worked before/after trace proving a fix reduced PSI and frame misses.
discovered_connections: Day 51's direct reclaim and compaction stalls become measurable through PSI some/full windows.
Day 50's watermark breaches are upstream triggers, while PSI is the downstream stall symptom.
Day 49's refault and swap evidence is required to distinguish healthy reclaim from thrashing.
PSI can bridge kernel VM counters and Android user experience when aligned with FrameTimeline.
